newsitem.title: USA: Meyer says would like to see banker on Fed board.
newsitem.headline: Meyer says would like to see banker on Fed board.

text.p: Naming a banker to fill one of two upcoming vacancies on the Federal Reserve Board might be useful as it would add to the diversity of backgrounds, Fed Governor Laurence Meyer said Thursday.

"I think a governor with banking experience would be desirable," Meyer told reporters following a speech to the Charlotte Economics Club here. "I would like to see a certain diversity of backgrounds on the board."

Two Fed governors, Lawrence Lindsey and Janet Yellen, have announced their intentions to step down. Lindsey will take up a job at the American Enterprise Institute and Yellen was nominated by President Clinton to head the Council of Economic Advisers.
The Clinton administration said last week it was in the early stages of looking for candidates to fill the two vacancies at the Fed.
